90% margin of error for Mining_Employment_Share, from Census's formula for a derived proportion (ACS handbook 2020, ch. 8, formula 6) using the S2403 MOEs. When it is at least the share itself, the share is not distinguishable from zero (Census's CV > 0.61 line) and the dashboard says so. Census's CV-based reliability rules are unstable for shares under 5% (National Research Council 2007, p. 67), so no reliability tier is given.
County 5-year percentage change in total resident population.

Estimated proportion of school-age children (ages 5-17) living in families below the federal poverty line. Not a true poverty rate (Census): the first count includes only children related to the householder, in families in poverty; the second, all children 5-17 (foster children, other unrelated children and children in group quarters are in the second only). The dashboards label it "School-age children in poverty (Census est.)".
Total population of the SAIPE district behind the child poverty estimate (SAEPOVALL_PT); for a charter or early-childhood center, its surrounding district's. It sets the estimate's error band.

Low end of Census's approximate 90% range for Child_Poverty_Rate: rate x (1 - 1.645 x CV), floored at 0. CV is Census's median relative error for districts of that size (0.67 under 2,500 people down to 0.15 at 65,000+; "Quantifying Relative Error in the School District Estimates", revised 2025-12-17), which Census calls an approximate upper bound. Census publishes no margin of error for one district.
High end of the same range: rate x (1 + 1.645 x CV), capped at 1. See Child_Poverty_Low.
Release year of federal Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE) data.
Actual average total compensation paid across all employed certified classroom teachers in the district.
Actual average base contract salary paid across all employed certified classroom teachers in the district.

Set only when Child_Poverty_Rate is a stand-in: for a school with no SAIPE geography of its own (charter, private, tribal or early-childhood), the rate of the school district it sits in, named here ('Surrounding district: ...'; a split town's two districts combined by their counts of children). Share of students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch: eligible students over enrollment, summed over the entity's schools that report.
